notes: One target: the container from docker-compose.yml. 127.0.0.1 is the honest value here — the container publishes on loopback, so this is not a placeholder standing in for a machine somewhere.

'service_name' is a SERVICE LABEL, not a database. This is the single most important thing to get right on SQL Server: collection always connects to master and the metric SQL issues its own USE. Putting a database name here — or letting the label be used as one — fails every SQL Server target at once with 'Cannot open database ... requested by the login'. The rule is enforced in db_ops/metrics/executor.py, not left to configuration.
'database_names' is what the per-database metrics iterate over. It is a list of real databases, unlike 'service_name'.
'major_version' picks the metric variant. 16 is SQL Server 2022; anything 11 or above gets the modern query, and older instances get the legacy_2008r2 variant instead of failing to parse.

'cmd_access' is absent, so no OS metric is attempted. Reaching into the container to measure the laptop's CPU and reporting it under this instance's name would be a lie, and the toolkit refuses that shape rather than doing it quietly.

db_instances.note: Throwaway container. env is 'lab', which is what lets LOCK_BLOCKING_SESSIONS downgrade its severity — see the report_policy on that metric in metric_definitions.json.
